claims.claim: Every connected cograph other than a singleton or a graph with exactly one universal vertex is equivalent to the zero game.
claims.evidence: A connected non-singleton cograph has a canonical join decomposition. If it has at least two universal vertices, those two vertices form a pairing dominating set. If it has none, every join block has size at least two; two vertices from one block and two from another form two disjoint pairs whose closed-neighborhood intersections cover every vertex. Remark 9 from the source then gives contextual equivalence to zero.
claims.witness: For blocks X,Y, choose distinct a,b in X and c,d in Y. Vertices of X lie in N[c]∩N[d], while every vertex outside X lies in N[a]∩N[b].
claims.search_method: Independent cotree case analysis, followed by exhaustive source-game minimax over all 535 labeled cographs on at most five vertices.

claims.claim: SHVG on cographs is polynomially equivalent to an explicit open-or-delete scoring game on rooted forests.
claims.evidence: For a connected component with unique universal vertex u, exchanging any proposed move in that component with u cannot hurt Maker and cannot help Maker when performed by Breaker. Breaker ownership of u leaves a zero-valued component. After Maker owns u, a twin pair in C-u can be assigned one vertex to each player using Theorem 13; this spoils u and makes every remaining happiness condition identical to that in C-u. Thus Maker opens the child forest and Breaker deletes the component. The recursive inverse using a disjoint K2 ballast and a new universal vertex is a linear-size cograph construction.
claims.witness: The exact checker preserved the distinction between prize leaves and nullary non-prize internal nodes and found no mismatch between graph minimax and the reduced forest for every labeled cograph through five vertices, including post-universal positions and arbitrary graph contexts through three vertices.
claims.search_method: Reproved the universal-move exchange and twin reduction from the source rules; checked the forward reduction, inverse model, and contextual behavior by exhaustive minimax.

claims.claim: The cograph game is linear-time solvable when every tree in the reduced forest has outdegree at most two.
claims.evidence: Bottom-up contextual induction leaves only A and zero. An internal node with zero or one A-type child has both starting scores zero and is contextually zero by Theorem 6. With two A-type children, opening exposes A+A, which is the constant game 1, so the node is exactly A. After one traversal, a forest with z surviving A-types has scores (ceil(z/2),floor(z/2)). Cotree construction and this labeling take linear input time.
claims.witness: All 398 unlabeled rooted trees through ten nodes having outdegree at most two, plus sampled forests of them, matched the asserted A/zero classification exactly.
claims.search_method: Contextual induction on rooted-tree height and exhaustive unrestricted open-or-delete minimax.

claims.claim: Reduced forests of height one—equivalently, disjoint unions of stars and isolated vertices after zero components are removed—admit an O(n^2) exact algorithm.
claims.evidence: For j≤k, the exchange induction establishes that deleting the k-star is no worse for Breaker than deleting the j-star, while opening the k-star is no worse for Maker than opening the j-star. The induction closes under all three move classes: deleting a star, opening a star, and taking an exposed prize. Hence only the largest star is needed in each recurrence. There are O(rK)=O(n²) feasible (i,l) states and constant work per state.
claims.witness: Unrestricted minimax agreed with the largest-star recurrence on 1,058,148 states with up to seven stars, leaf counts 1–12, and up to twenty initially exposed prizes; no omitted star choice improved either player.
claims.search_method: Checked the exchange inequalities inductively and compared the restricted recurrence with a recurrence enumerating every legal star choice.

claims.claim: If q is the number of vertices of outdegree at least three in a reduced rooted forest, every residual forest occurring in play is equivalent, up to the integer score already secured, to a branching-core state (S,l), where l counts prize-leaf games and S is an antichain of at most q original nodes, each rooting a remaining component that contains a branching vertex.
claims.evidence: Every subtree containing no branching vertex has maximum outdegree two and can be replaced contextually by A or zero. The unreplaced active roots are descendants exposed by prior openings, hence form an antichain. Their rooted subtrees are disjoint and each contains an original branching vertex, yielding an injection from S into the q branching vertices. The stated Maker, Breaker, and prize transitions preserve this invariant and the score exactly.
claims.witness: The branching-core quotient matched unrestricted minimax for every one of the 1,205 unlabeled rooted trees through ten nodes and for sampled multi-tree forests; the antichain-size bound also held in every generated state.
claims.search_method: Invariant proof using disjoint descendant subtrees, supplemented by exhaustive quotient-versus-full-game comparison.

claims.claim: The rooted-forest game, and hence SHVG on cographs, has an exact XP algorithm parameterized by q, the number of outdegree-at-least-three vertices in the reduced forest; in particular it is polynomial-time solvable for every fixed q.
claims.evidence: The displayed recurrences enumerate every move from a branching-core state. Opening v replaces it with its marked children and a(v) A-types; deleting v removes its component; a prize move removes one A and adds one point only for Maker. Total represented original nodes plus l strictly decreases. Since |S|≤q and 0≤l≤n, at most (n+1)Σ_{i=0}^q binom(n,i) states occur, giving n^{O(q)} time and polynomial time for fixed q.
claims.witness: Direct evaluation of the memoized branching-core recurrence agreed with unrestricted rooted-forest minimax throughout the exhaustive small-tree test set.
claims.search_method: Verified transition completeness, acyclicity, state count, and exact values independently.

claims.claim: The pair of standalone scores (Ms,Bs) is insufficient as a cotree dynamic-programming state.
claims.evidence: P3 and K1,3 both have standalone scores (1,0), but their behavior under the same union operation differs. Therefore a union-node computation receiving only the two child score pairs cannot distinguish the two inputs and cannot always return the correct result.
claims.witness: Exact values are (Ms,Bs)(P3+P3)=(1,1) and (Ms,Bs)(P3+K1,3)=(2,1), although each component supplied to the union has state (1,0).
claims.search_method: Direct exact minimax on the corresponding rooted stars and their sums.

claims.claim: For every m≥1, the rooted stars S_{2m} and S_{2m+1} have the same standalone scores (m,0), but adjoining one prize leaf A gives scores (m,1) and (m+1,1), respectively.
claims.evidence: Maker opening S_k leaves Breaker on k prizes, giving floor(k/2), while Breaker deletes its root for zero. In A+S_k, Maker obtains max(1,floor((k+1)/2)) and Breaker obtains min(floor(k/2),1). Substitution of k=2m and k=2m+1 gives exactly the claimed pairs for every m≥1.
claims.witness: The four formulas were checked by unrestricted exact minimax for every 1≤m≤64 without a mismatch.
claims.search_method: Closed-form evaluation of every initial move, followed by finite-range exact verification.

claims.claim: For every N there are N pairwise contextually inequivalent rooted-tree games on at most 2N+4 forest nodes that all have standalone scores (1,0); thus the failure of the (Ms,Bs) state is unbounded.
claims.evidence: For F_m with children A,A,S_{2m}, opening exposes the constant game 1 plus S_{2m}, so F_m has scores (1,0) and size 2m+4. For r<s, context S_{2s} gives Breaker-first value 1 in both cases, while Maker-first values are max(s,r+1)=s for F_r and max(s,s+1)=s+1 for F_s. Thus every pair is separated by a legal rooted-star context.
claims.witness: For m≤24 the checker confirmed every F_m=(1,0) and every proposed pairwise separator; the symbolic calculation applies for arbitrary N.
claims.search_method: Exact symbolic evaluation of both opening choices and both deletion choices, supplemented by exhaustive parameter checks.

target_evidence: The draft establishes an exact cograph-to-forest reduction, two tractable subclasses, an XP algorithm for fixed branching parameter q, and an unbounded obstruction to a two-score cotree state. These are material correct advances, but q may grow with the input. The draft supplies neither a polynomial-time algorithm for unrestricted cographs nor a matching hardness theorem, and its final writeup explicitly says so. Therefore it does not fully resolve the exact source target, while its PARTIAL resolution claim is accurate.
